name: Revvity
description: Revvity sells research tools and diagnostic tests in two roughly equal halves. Life Sciences ($1.43 billion) sells reagents, antibodies (BioLegend), instruments, imaging and Signals software to drug and biotech researchers. Diagnostics ($1.42 billion) sells testing kits and instruments to hospital and public-health labs, led by prenatal and newborn screening and autoimmune and infectious-disease immunodiagnostics (EUROIMMUN, T-SPOT). Standard sector data files it under Health Care Equipment, but the 10-K describes it as a health-science tools and diagnostics company, so its closest peers are life-science tools businesses. 61% of revenue comes from outside the U.S.; China alone is $425 million (15%).

employees.note: Roughly 80% outside the United States; about 2,000 sales and service representatives in about 40 countries; products marketed in more than 160 countries.

businessLines.name: Life Sciences
businessLines.how: Sells reagents, antibodies and assays (BioLegend), instruments and imaging systems, and software (Signals) to pharma, biotech, CROs and academic labs; consumables are repeat purchases, instruments are one-time, software is subscription.

businessLines.name: Diagnostics
businessLines.how: Sells instruments, reagents and assay platforms to hospitals and diagnostic labs, especially prenatal and newborn screening (reproductive health) and immunodiagnostics (EUROIMMUN autoimmune and allergy tests, T-SPOT TB); instrument placement then recurring test kits.

brands.name: BioLegend, Signals, Revvity Signals
brands.note: Life Sciences brands (BioLegend antibodies and LEGENDplex; ELISA MAX); revenue not broken out.

brands.name: EUROIMMUN, T-SPOT, ViaCord, IDS, DELFIA, NeoBase, chemagic
brands.note: Diagnostics brands (the 10-K lists dozens); revenue not broken out beyond Immunodiagnostics $869.9M and Reproductive health $555.0M.
